newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slightly lower, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: German call money slightly lower, market quiet.

text.p: German call money was quoted slightly lower in a quiet market on Thursday, trading at rates of 3.00/03 percent compared with 3.03/05 percent on Wednesday.
But dealers said the market was quiet and that there was no particular change in the trend. Euromarket rates were seen as the main influence pushing rates in the domestic market lower.

"Call money is maybe two or three ticks lower than yesterday, but nothing has changed in principle in the situation," a trader said. Banks held reserves of 41.3 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Wednesday for an average of 41.5 billion for the first 16 days of July.
Banks took up only a negligible amount at the 4.50 percent Lombard emergency lending rate.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was calculated at 3.05400 compared with 3.07575 percent.
The 12-month FIBOR rate, which had edged higher in the last day or so, eased back to 3.34425 from Wednesday's 3.34933.
